requirements.text: The system SHALL accept a local directory path containing Markdown (.md) files as input and recursively discover all .md files within that directory tree.
requirements.rationale: Core ingestion capability required by goal 1; relies on assumption A1 that notes are stored as individual .md files in a local directory.

requirements.text: The system SHALL parse each discovered Markdown file using at least CommonMark-compliant syntax and produce a corresponding HTML page that preserves the original formatting and structure (headings, lists, code blocks, emphasis, images, links).
requirements.rationale: Directly supports goal 2 (preserve Markdown formatting) and constraint CNS2 (standard Markdown syntax).

requirements.text: The build output SHALL consist exclusively of static files (HTML, CSS, JS, and associated assets) that can be served by any standard HTTP file server or static hosting provider without a server-side runtime or database.
requirements.rationale: Satisfies constraint CNS1 and goal 6; aligns with non-goal of no dynamic server-rendered application.

requirements.text: The system SHALL generate a client-side full-text search index at build time and embed it in the output so that users can search note titles and body text entirely in the browser without server-side processing.
requirements.rationale: Supports goal 3 (full-text search) and assumption A4 (client-side search to keep the site static). Maps to success metric on search returning relevant results.

requirements.text: The system SHALL extract tags from each note using at least one supported convention (YAML front matter `tags` field or inline `#tag` syntax) and generate a tag index page listing all tags, plus individual per-tag pages listing all notes associated with each tag.
requirements.rationale: Supports goal 4 (tag-based browsing) and assumption A3. Maps to success metric that selecting a tag shows all associated notes.

requirements.text: Each generated note page SHALL display the tags associated with that note as navigable links to the corresponding tag pages.
requirements.rationale: Completes the tag browsing loop described in goal 4 and the success metric requiring each note page to display its tags.

requirements.text: The system SHALL detect internal links between notes (at minimum, standard Markdown relative links to other .md files) and resolve them to the correct generated HTML pages in the output.
requirements.rationale: Supports goal 5 (detect and render internal links). Relates to assumption A2 and blocking question Q1; at minimum relative-path Markdown links must work.

requirements.text: For every note that is the target of at least one internal link, the generated page SHALL include a 'Backlinks' section listing all notes that link to it, rendered as clickable navigation links.
requirements.rationale: Directly supports goal 5 (backlinks / 'linked from' sections) and the success metric on backlink generation.

requirements.text: The system SHALL provide a command-line interface (CLI) that accepts at minimum an input directory path and an output directory path, and executes the full build pipeline.
requirements.rationale: Assumption A5 confirms a CLI build workflow is acceptable; Q10 asks about interface but CLI is the minimum viable interface to trigger builds.

requirements.text: The build process SHALL complete without errors for a valid input set of Markdown files and produce a usable output directory, or report clear, actionable error messages on failure.
requirements.rationale: Maps directly to the first success metric (build completes without errors) and general usability.

requirements.text: Every Markdown file in the input set (not explicitly excluded by configuration) SHALL have a corresponding HTML page in the output.
requirements.rationale: Maps to success metric that all Markdown files are rendered into accessible HTML pages.

requirements.text: The generated site SHALL load and function correctly in the current stable releases of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge without JavaScript errors that block core functionality (navigation, search, backlinks, tags).
requirements.rationale: Maps to success metric requiring the site to load and function in modern browsers without errors.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD support wiki-style internal links (e.g., [[Note Title]]) in addition to standard Markdown relative links, resolving them to the appropriate generated pages.
requirements.rationale: Assumption A2 notes wiki-style links as a likely convention; Q1 highlights this as high-impact. Supporting both conventions greatly increases compatibility with popular note-taking tools like Obsidian.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD support GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) extensions including tables, strikethrough, task lists, and fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting.
requirements.rationale: Q6 asks about Markdown flavor; GFM is the most common superset and widely expected by users. Enhances goal 2 (preserve formatting).

requirements.text: The generated site SHOULD include a home/landing page and a navigation structure providing access to an all-notes listing, the tag index, and the search feature.
requirements.rationale: Q4 identifies information architecture as high-impact. A minimal navigation structure is necessary for the site to be usable and discoverable.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD allow configuration of a base URL / path prefix so the generated site can be deployed to a subdirectory (e.g., GitHub Pages project sites).
requirements.rationale: Q5 highlights deployment targets; base URL configuration is essential for GitHub Pages and similar hosts where the site is not at the root.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD warn at build time when an internal link target cannot be resolved (broken link), listing the source file and link text, without failing the build by default.
requirements.rationale: Q8 asks about broken link handling. Warning without failing is the most pragmatic default; supports iterative authoring while surfacing issues.

requirements.text: Full-text search results SHALL be returned and rendered in under 500 ms for collections of up to 1,000 notes on a modern consumer device.
requirements.rationale: Q3 asks about scale; 1,000 notes is a reasonable default target. The success metric requires search to remain responsive at the confirmed target scale.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD normalize tags by lowercasing and trimming whitespace so that equivalent tags (e.g., 'JavaScript' and 'javascript') are merged into a single tag page.
requirements.rationale: Q2 asks about tag normalization rules. Without normalization, duplicate tag pages degrade the browsing experience.

requirements.text: The system SHOULD allow users to exclude specific files or directories from the build via a configuration file or CLI option.
requirements.rationale: Supports the success metric caveat 'excluding explicitly configured ignores' and common user need to skip drafts or template files.

requirements.text: The system COULD provide an incremental build mode that only regenerates pages for notes that have changed since the last build.
requirements.rationale: Q7 identifies incremental builds as a medium-impact enhancement. Improves developer experience for large collections but is not essential for correctness.

requirements.text: The system COULD provide a local development server with live-reload/watch mode that automatically rebuilds and refreshes the browser when source files change.
requirements.rationale: Q7 mentions watch mode for local preview. Greatly improves authoring workflow but is not required for the core build-and-deploy use case.

requirements.text: The generated site COULD include an interactive graph visualization showing the link relationships between notes.
requirements.rationale: Q8 asks about graph views. A graph view enhances discoverability but is a significant feature beyond the core backlinks requirement.

requirements.text: The system COULD support user-selectable themes or custom CSS injection to allow visual customization of the generated site.
requirements.rationale: Q9 asks about theming requirements. Theming improves personalization but is not essential for the core functionality of search, tags, and backlinks.

requirements.text: The system COULD render outgoing links on each note page as a dedicated section alongside the backlinks section, providing bidirectional link context.
requirements.rationale: Q8 asks whether to expose outgoing links. Showing outgoing links alongside backlinks enhances navigation but backlinks alone satisfy the stated goals.
